detail:
Mayo Clinic describes Sjögren's treatment as depending on which parts of the body are affected, and notes that many symptoms respond well to self-care measures. Sources describe artificial tears and eye lubricants, raising indoor humidity, and avoiding air blowing into the face for dry eyes. For dry mouth, measures include sipping water through the day, sugar-free gum or candies to prompt saliva flow, and artificial saliva products.

Because dry mouth increases the risk of cavities and tooth loss, Mayo Clinic describes oral health steps such as brushing and flossing after meals and dental appointments at least every six months. Prescription medicines clinicians may use include eye drops that lessen eye inflammation, medicines that increase saliva production, antifungal medicines for mouth yeast infections, and, for whole-body symptoms, medicines such as hydroxychloroquine or immune-suppressing medicines. A minor procedure to seal tear ducts, called punctal occlusion, may help preserve tears in some cases.

Tabs is not endorsing or verifying this material. Talk to your doctor about ongoing Sjögren's management.
summary: Mayo Clinic describes Sjögren's care, from self-care for dry eyes and dry mouth and regular dental care, to prescription eye drops, saliva-stimulating medicines, and medicines for whole-body symptoms.
takeaways: many symptoms respond to self-care sources describe, like artificial tears
dry mouth raises cavity risk, so regular dental care matters
prescription options can reduce eye inflammation or increase saliva
never start, stop, or change medicines without your doctor
title: Managing Sjögren's syndrome day to day
